To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

maltose transport is independent of galactoside or glucose permease function, that galactoside transport is independent of maltose permease function, but that glucose transport is partially dependent on galactoside and maltose permease.
maltose transport is not affected by the concentration of glucose in the growth medium, and that maltose transport does affect glucose transport in the same cells.

maltose transport is inhibited by glucose and galactosides in cells possessing both maltose permease and galactosidase permease, whereas glucose transport is unaffected by maltose or galacstosides in cells with galactoside transport.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of maltose transport with the transport of other sugars.
the transport of sugars by the cell.
the transport of sugars and sugar analogs by the cell surface of Escherichiacoli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the glucose permease system is a more abundant system in the cell membrane than either of the maltose or galatoside systems.
the glucose permease is the major permease system on the cell surface, and the maltose and galac-toside systems are present in much smaller numbers.
the glucose permease system in cells grown on maltose or lactose is more numerous than that for maltose or lactoside, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glucose transport system is the most important one in the cell, and the others are secondary.

the number of maltose transport systems on the surface of the cell is equal to the number of glucose transport systems and that the number of galactoside transport systems is equal to the sum of the number of maltrose and glucose transport systems.
glucose permease systems are present on the surface of cells of Eschericha coli in a much larger number than are the maltose or galacotside permease systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glucose transport system is more sensitive to glucose than to galactosides, whereas the galactoside transport system is more responsive to galactoside than to glucose.
the maltose transporter is the most efficient transporter in E. coli.
, in cells possessing two different sugar permeases, the transport of each substrate is not influenced by the presence of the other substrate.
